as_read: Null for cardiovascular outcomes: Cochrane and two other meta-analyses find no cardiovascular benefit of raising omega-6 fats, apart from a low-quality myocardial infarction signal and lower total cholesterol.

quote.text: We found no evidence that increasing omega-6 fats reduces cardiovascular outcomes other than MI, where 53 people may need to increase omega-6 fat intake to prevent 1 person from experiencing MI.

proposed_decision_text: All four labels print Omega-6 Fatty Acids as a summary row of an oil, not as an added active: EfaGold hemp oil 8.5 g, and MEGA 3/6/9 oil blend 705 mg on three labels, each with linoleic acid and gamma-linolenic acid rows beside it. The Cochrane review (30488422, 19 RCTs, 6461 participants, 12 of linoleic acid and 7 of supplemental gamma-linolenic acid) found increased omega-6 fats may make little or no difference to all-cause mortality or cardiovascular events. It also reports conflicting signals: a possible reduction in myocardial infarction (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.02, low quality) and lower total cholesterol. A later meta-analysis in atherosclerotic disease (38224465) found omega-6 had no significant effect on mortality or cardiovascular events, with low-quality evidence. A meta-analysis of linoleic acid trials (23386268) showed no cardiovascular benefit. So the evidence conflicts on surrogates with no clear clinical benefit. Most of these trials had omega-6 fats displacing saturated or monounsaturated fats at dietary amounts, so this is the best available evidence rather than a test of these exact products.
